Our story

Blessed & Fortunate

The bride · Xitsonga

Nyiko

Fortunate · from Bushbuckridge

Nyiko means gift. A scientist, a woman of faith, and the one who takes all the pictures.

The groom · Tshivenda

Rotondwa

Blessing

Rotondwa speaks of being honoured. Caring to his family, loved by his friends, a walking library, and a loyal Pirates supporter.

  1. 2018 10 March

    The first picture

    A friend's 21st birthday. She was organising the transport group, which is how his number ended up in her phone. She took pictures with everyone that day, him included, and thought nothing of it.

    She later confessed that she used to dodge him in biochemistry. He sat front left and left by the front door, so she sat on the other side and used the back. Then he replied to her status, and they became friends.

  2. 2019 19 January

    Two apples and an ice cream

    Their first official date: two apples and an ice cream she spilled. Their classmates only found out on his graduation day, when she showed up in a red dress and he graduated with distinction. He took her to her first soccer match, still hoping to make her a Pirates fan.

    In November they parted ways, but they chose to stay friends.

  3. 2020 The friendship year

    A promise and a poem

    Lockdown kept them apart, but he greeted her every day, they swapped selfies, and he helped her plan life after honours. When he faced the fears that had kept them apart, they made a promise to each other for their marriage, and he wrote her a poem.

    They came back together in October. He visited once, in November, and that visit gave them their only picture of the year.

  4. 2021 The reunion year

    Lunch dates between campuses

    Both doing their master's, on neighbouring campuses: genetics and computational work for him, health sciences for her. They met for lunch, she took the pictures, and he patiently posed. When a tooth abscess floored her, he helped nurse her back to health.

  5. 2022 July

    Meeting the parents

    A week before his master's graduation, he told his parents: “Her name is Fortunate. She's from Bushbuckridge, and I want to marry this girl.” In his home, whoever you introduce is the one you marry.

    On a freezing July day, his mother's first question was “Are you born again?” That conversation became a bond: today she prays for Fortunate, and for her friends by name.

  6. 2023–26 To be continued

    [More chapters coming]

    [The proposal, the lobola negotiations, and his graduation on 7 December 2026.]

  7. 2027 March

    Venda meets Tsonga

    Their traditional wedding in Mpumalanga. Not just love: Godly love. And you are invited.

Tshivenda & Xitsonga

Learn a little of both

Two families will be speaking two languages on the day. A few words go a long way, so greet the elders in their own tongue.

English Tshivenda Xitsonga
HelloNdaa (said by men) · Aa (said by women)Xewani
Thank youNdo livhuwaNdza khensa
LoveLufunoRirhandzu
We welcome youRi a ni ṱanganedzaHi mi amukela
MarriageMbinganoVukati
Bride, daughter-in-lawMuselwaN’wingi
Son-in-lawMukwashaMukon’wana

On this day Nyiko becomes muselwa to the Venda family, and Rotondwa becomes mukon’wana to the Tsonga family.

On the day

What to expect from both sides

Dance

Venda · The joyful malende circle of song and clapping, and the tshikona reed-pipe dance.

Tsonga · The swing of the xibelani skirt and the stamping of the men’s muchongolo.

Wear shoes you can dance in. You will be pulled into the circle.

From both kitchens

Venda · Tshidzimba, samp cooked with beans and groundnuts, and mashonzha, mopane worms.

Tsonga · Tihove, samp mashed with peanuts, and matomani, the same mopane worms by their Xitsonga name.

Menu: [to be confirmed]

Respect & joy

Venda · You may see women greet elders with u losha, a graceful low greeting of respect.

Tsonga · Expect the women to welcome the couple with ululation, song and a dance of celebration.

In both homes, elders are greeted first and served first.

Dress code · Traditional attire

Burgundy & beige, Venda meets Tsonga

This is a traditional wedding, so please come in traditional attire in our colours. Venda or Tsonga, or wear both.

Burgundy
Beige
Venda & Tsonga prints

Ladies

A Tsonga xibelani with an nceka, or a Venda minwenda, in burgundy or beige. Add a headwrap and beadwork to finish the look.

Gentlemen

A traditional shirt in Venda stripes or Tsonga print, in burgundy or beige, worn with plain trousers. A beaded necklace or a draped cloth over the shoulder completes it.

The finishing touch

Mix the two cultures: a Venda-striped wrap with Tsonga beads, or a xibelani with a Venda-print top. Beaded bangles and necklaces are welcome on everyone.
